entries.reason: Not an absence. This is the LABEL on the disclosure that holds the machine's own words, and the `??` chooses between a caller's own label and the console's standard one. It asserts nothing about any record; a card with nothing to disclose renders no disclosure at all, because the component takes `detail` and returns null when it is absent. The words are the ones §9A.2 names for this slot on every surface.

Not an absence. `needsYou.needed` is already TRUE at this point — the caller has asserted the card needs the owner — and the `??` only chooses wording when the caller named no specific action. So it stands in front of a known YES, never in front of an unknown, and 'Needs you: Yes — a decision from you' is the least specific TRUE sentence rather than a guess about a record. Appears twice: once in NeedsYouLine, once in DefinedTile, which render the same fact in two shapes.

Not an absence. The default fires when a link carries no LABEL, and a link with no label is one on the candidate's own domain — where "official site" and "campaign site" describe exactly the thing that IS present. The label exists for the two cases where those words would be false: RULING 122's page a party publishes about a candidate, and RULING 145's campaign presence on a platform, both of which name their host instead. So the ?? is choosing between two true descriptions of a link that is there, never standing in front of one that is missing — and when there is no link, neither branch renders at all.
